title: Sample 19-6: Shaped Letter Puzzles

illustrates.quote: f. For irregularly shaped puzzles, do not insert spaces between letters; follow print for letter placement.

blocks.text:
whiskers   small
ears        gray
tail       brown
nose       cheese
furry      cat
trap
blocks.features: A 2-column, 11-word word-bank (to be found inside the mouse-shaped grid below), in uncontracted braille (e.g. 'small' is spelled out letter-by-letter, s-m-a-l-l, rather than contracting to its usual one-cell whole-word sign) — column alignment is not reproducible (F-219).

blocks.text: The puzzle is shaped like a mouse.
(an irregularly, mouse-shaped word-search grid of letters, 9 rows, following print's own letter placement with no inserted spaces per 19.6.1f)
blocks.features: Not braille-buildable: the model has no mechanism for an irregular, print-driven letter grid whose OWN leading indentation varies row to row (F-217/219).

print.notes: A two-column word-bank list, a transcriber's note explaining the puzzle's mouse shape, and the shaped word-search grid itself.
print.printFeatures: Word bank (2 columns), transcriber's note, irregularly-shaped (mouse-outline) letter grid.

braille.notes: Byte-identical between run A and run B, and independently re-derived from source-lines 15454-15481. The whole shaped grid (lines 11-19) is wrapped in one grade-1, capitalized-word passage ('""=;;;,,,' / '""=,\';\''); the word-bank list (lines 1-6) and the transcriber's note (lines 8) sit OUTSIDE that passage, before it.

resolution: Braille unchanged (A and B agree, byte-identical; independently re-derived, matches exactly). Print side reconciled: the transcriber's note is back-translation-verified verbatim; the word-bank list and the shaped grid are both documented as not braille-buildable (F-217/219/222), matching both runs' own general understanding. Print description corrected 23 Sep 2026 (see printCorrections).
